import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 13

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture13

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 13](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ diam(G) + max_{v ∈ V} l(v) - 1`, where `diam(G)` is the diameter
of `G` and `l(v) = indepNeighborsCard G v` is the independence number of the
neighbourhood of `v`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture13 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    letI maxL := (Finset.univ.image (fun v => indepNeighborsCard G v)).max' (by simp)
    (G.diam : ℝ) + (maxL : ℝ) - 1 ≤ b G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The largest induced bipartite subgraph invariant `b G` is nonneg for any graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₂`, all vertices have degree 1, so `indepNeighborsCard` at vertex 0 is 0
(the neighbourhood of 0 consists of only vertex 1, which has no independent edges). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).maxDegree = 1 := by decide +native

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture13

findings.description: The docstring of the anonymous example at lines 53–56 incorrectly says that `indepNeighborsCard` at vertex 0 of K₂ is 0, referring to 'independent edges'. This invariant counts independent vertices: the neighbourhood consists of one vertex and has independence number 1. The actual example proves only `maxDegree = 1`, which is correct. I verified `indepNeighborsCard (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) 0 = 1` in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaViña, Some History of the Development of Graffiti, Definitions 3.3 and 3.5, https://www.uhd.edu/documents/academics/sciences/history.pdf: independence number is the cardinality of a largest independent vertex set, and local independence is the independence number of the subgraph induced by a vertex's neighbours. These definitions give local independence 1 in K₂.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the comment with `/-- In K₂, the maximum degree is 1. -/`, matching the existing example. If a neighbourhood-independence test is desired, add a separate example asserting `indepNeighborsCard (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) 0 = 1`.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly assumes `[Nontrivial α]`, while the author's formulation says 'simple connected graph' without explicitly excluding the singleton graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness excludes the empty graph. For a singleton graph, the diameter and all neighbourhood independence numbers are 0, and b = 1, so the inequality is automatically true. Thus the assertion for nontrivial finite connected graphs is equivalent to the assertion for all finite connected graphs. An explicit universe-polymorphic equivalence was proved in `/workspace/review/equivalence.lean`; its axioms contain no `sorryAx` and it does not invoke the conjecture.

review.notes: The cited legacy website and its cms.uhd.edu alias were unavailable. The author's own survey supplies the identical inequality as Conjecture 24 on p. 30, identifies this list as part of Written on the Wall II, and states that Waller and DeLaViña proved it. Consequently the main statement and its `research solved` tag agree with the recovered primary source. The invariant definitions, finite suprema, maximum, diameter defaults, quantifiers, and real arithmetic were checked. Lean boundary tests passed, as did an independent enumeration of every connected labelled simple graph on at most six vertices. Review artifacts are under `/workspace/review/`; repository files were not edited.
